items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: Mildred asked me to do something for her and that's how they kicked the whole thing off on me, because I never really thought of being a professional writer.

ctx.x: And I think that he probably did that too. He confesses to not having enough patience to do it.

I began, at that time, as (Cyrinus) Tootie did, for Barnet and I guess Mildred and Red sort of liked it and Mildred asked me to do something for her and that's how they kicked the whole thing off on me, because I never really thought of being a professional writer. I hadn't thought of being a professional anything at that point.
I was making money to go back to college. Meanwhile, I didn't know what for either. I liked to play and it had been my complete life, as you can tell, from the beginning.
